speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with persistent vomiting and chest pain; to help me understand the severity and cause, can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if the pain radiates to your arm, jaw, or back?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Spontaneous Esophageal Rupture).

The combination of forceful vomiting after heavy alcohol consumption, followed by retching, choking, and subsequent chest pain is the classic presentation for esophageal rupture. I will now request imaging to confirm the diagnosis.

REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray (upright and lateral decubitus views).
